facts.fact: 她抹掉脸上的灰、靠墙缓了一下，过了一会儿才意识到自己在哪儿
facts.anchor: It took me a moment to realise where I was.

facts.fact: 她注意到倾斜的天花板和开在天花板上的窗，头一阵发晕——她在邻居的卧室里，在楼上
facts.anchor: Then I noticed the slanting ceiling and the window set into it. My head spun. I was in her bedroom. Upstairs.

facts.fact: 不知怎么的，她从我家的地下室，到了 1a 的一楼
facts.anchor: Somehow, I had got from my basement to the first floor of 1a.

facts.fact: 这房间装饰得极其讲究
facts.anchor: It was lusciously decorated.

facts.fact: 缀着小金星的透明窗帘罩着一张铺了好几层华贵织物的床：深酒红缎面床单上压着厚羽绒被，一条手感厚实的雪尼尔盖毯，床尾随意搭着一块奶油色毛皮
facts.anchor: Sheer curtains dotted with little golden stars enveloped a bed layered in sumptuous fabrics; a thick feather duvet in deep burgundy sateen sheets, a tactile chenille throw, and a creamy fur tossed casually over the bottom.

facts.fact: 一打枕头堆在一只贝壳形状的软包床头板周围
facts.anchor: A dozen pillows were piled around a padded headboard shaped like a shell.

facts.fact: 一串暖色小灯在床周围照出一圈柔和的光晕
facts.anchor: A string of warm fairy lights lit the bed with a gentle halo.

facts.fact: 门把上搭着一条带香味的围巾，还带着体温，把空气熏成浓郁的花香——就是她昨天系在邻居门把手上的那条格子围巾
facts.anchor: Draped over the door, a perfumed scarf—still body-warm—scented the air with a heady, floral aroma. It was the same tartan scarf I’d tied onto her door handle yesterday.

facts.fact: 邻居最近来过；也许她能找到更多关于她的东西：一条线索、一个弱点、一个让她停下来的钥匙
facts.anchor: My neighbour had been here recently. Maybe I could find out more about her, a clue, a weakness, a key to making her stop.

facts.fact: 她沿着墙边挪，什么都不想碰，小心跨过一张干净的羊皮地毯——那张看上去比她自己那张软得多
facts.anchor: I edged along the wall, not wanting to touch anything, being careful to step over a pristine sheepskin rug—which somehow looked much softer than mine.

facts.fact: 她在床罩下看见一对银色蕾丝内裤和相配的胸罩；香水底下还有另一种气味，温热身体、汗和头发的气味，浓郁、动物性——她脸上发烫，对自己说："专心办事。"
facts.anchor: I felt the heat rise in my cheeks. Stay on task, I told myself.

facts.fact: 窗外世界不见了，像玻璃被黑色亮漆刷过
facts.anchor: The world outside was gone. It was as if the panes had been painted over with black gloss.

facts.fact: 是土：深色、压实的泥土，紧贴在玻璃上
facts.anchor: Soil. Dark, packed earth pressed up against the glass.

facts.fact: 她在底下，可她是从上到顶层出来的——这说不通："我怎么会在山里面？"
facts.anchor: I was underground. But I’d come out on the top floor. That didn’t make sense. How was I inside the hill?

facts.fact: 空心山，仙山
facts.anchor: Hollow hill. Fairy hill.

facts.fact: "天哪！我是被活埋了，这就是我的棺材。"六尺之下，独自在黑暗中，永远与所有人所有事隔绝——她开始过度换气
facts.anchor: Oh God! I was being buried alive and this was my coffin. Six feet under, alone in the dark, cut off from everyone and everything forever. I started to hyperventilate.

facts.fact: 她心里喊："这房子到底是什么鬼东西？"
facts.anchor: What the hell is this house?

facts.fact: 身后传来一个声音："这房子怎么了？"
facts.anchor: A voice came from behind me. “What about the house?”

facts.fact: 是 Fergus，低头看她，不眨眼，咧嘴笑，像大灰狼
facts.anchor: It was Fergus, looking down at me, unblinking, grinning, like the Big Bad Wolf.

facts.fact: 他站在五金杂货店的柜台后面；她四下一看，自己又站在货架之间了
facts.anchor: He was standing behind the counter at the hardware and supplies shop. I looked around. I was stood in the aisles again.

facts.fact: Fergus 说：他真的认识一个住在她那房子里的孩子，那是他最好的朋友；"但他并不是处变不惊——那部分是我编的。"
facts.anchor: I really did know a kid who lived in your house. He was my best friend. He wasn’t unflappable though. I made that bit up. He had this haunted look about him, always looking over his shoulders, like he was being hunted. Him and his mum.”

facts.fact: "他脸上总带着那种被鬼缠住的神情，不停回头看，像有人在猎他。他和他妈妈都是。"
facts.anchor: He had this haunted look about him, always looking over his shoulders, like he was being hunted.

facts.fact: 所有人都讨厌那孩子，觉得他妈妈是个势利婊子、他是个坏掉的怪胎；他们逼他跟她走；"然后我再也没见过他。"
facts.anchor: Everyone hated that kid. They thought his mum was a snooty whore and him a broken weirdo. They made him go with her. And then I never saw him again.

facts.fact: Fergus 说："只不过那不是你的房子，对吧？"
facts.anchor: Because it’s scary, your house. Only it’s not your house, is it?”

facts.fact: 他仍不眨眼，眼睛盯着她，笑还是那种大灰狼般饥饿的笑
facts.anchor: He still wasn’t blinking. His eyes continued to stare at me, his smile still a Big Bad Wolf-hungry grin.

facts.fact: "你当时想把它按在我手上，对吧？"他把手放在柜台上，把订书机头压上去
facts.anchor: “You wanted to press it to my hand, didn’t you?” He put his hand onto the counter and pushed the head of the stapler against it.

facts.fact: 他食指平滑地一扣，订书机开火，发出一声又响又湿的"咔嗒"
facts.anchor: With one smooth, squeeze of his trigger finger he fired the stapler and there was a loud, wet sch-unk.
